title: Improvements for the CSP dissector
description:
Some improvements for the CSP dissector:
- Decoding of SenderTimeStamp and Duration fields as relative time
- Decoding of Workload field as percentage
- URL fix

Do this in the else branch instead?

t still contains the value of timestamp 0xffffffffffffffffULL in the first part of the if-clause. So, when filtering for unknown durations, "Apply as filter" -> "Selected" creates "componentstatusprotocol.componentassociation_duration == 18446744073709.551615000". This will then retrieve all messages with unknown duration value (i.e. 0xffffffffffffffffULL). So, to make this work, it is necessary to convert timestamp to t. Is there a better solution for this?

Not very fond of these excedingly long defines like COMPONENTSTATUSREPORT_REPORTINTERVAL_OFFSET
Why not use offset and an integer for the length like most dissectors do...

commits_data.title: ComponentStatusProtocol dissector improvements.
commits_data.message:
ComponentStatusProtocol dissector improvements.

Changes in detail:
* Got rid of the macros.
* Decode SenderTimeStamp as relative time.
* Decode Duration field to relative time.
* Decode Workload field to percentage.
* Decode SenderTimeStamp as relative time.
* Decode ReportInterval field as relative time as well.
* Also decode details from SenderID and ReceiverID.
